findings.text: Carolina's Thursday article and official table agree Waller (toe) and Tremble (ribs) were limited; Freeling returned limited. Friday and game-status fields were unfilled at retrieval. These are two presentations of one team report, not independent predictive confirmations.
findings.confidence: HIGH for Thursday participation; future availability and workload unresolved

findings.text: The October 13 Raiders depth chart lists Bowers ahead of Mayer. Retrieved Week 6 injury pages list Bowers limited Wednesday and do not expose Thursday/Friday status. The dated October 10, 2025 Mayer-start story surfaced in search is a different season and was excluded from current-role inference.
findings.confidence: HIGH for displayed dated entries; insufficient for a Sunday promotion

findings.topic: Cowing does not inherit all vacated work
findings.text: Shanahan's October 15 transcript lists Samuel and Evans out of that day's practice and Kirk limited. The WR opportunity answer specifically discusses Watkins and Cooks. It does not establish Cowing's route participation or target share. Practice absence is not a final game designation.
findings.confidence: HIGH for transcript; LOW for any inferred receiver redistribution

findings.text: The Footballers Week 6 table reports Waller 19 targets/91 routes (20.9%) and Mayer 25/128 (19.5%) through Week 5. The arithmetic rounds correctly, but the underlying NGS counts were not independently reproduced. Different games, health and teammate contexts prevent ranking next-week value from these season rates alone.
findings.confidence: MEDIUM for attributed dataset; no validated player projection

findings.text: Fantasy Life's primer states 184 targets and 641 team targets but prints 27.4%. Those stated inputs give 184/641 = 28.705%, approximately 28.7%. The cause may be an editorial error or unstated denominator mismatch; this check does not establish the correct underlying season dataset or invalidate the broader route concept.

educational_lesson.central_method: Separate route access from target propensity; shrink noisy rates and expose uncertainty about future role.
educational_lesson.source_lesson: Anderson distinguishes routes from TPRR and warns that small samples, scheme, quarterback, injury and depth of target matter. His Week 6 method changes tier rules relative to positional medians and compares TPRR percentile with fantasy points per qualifying game. These are transparent descriptive choices, not demonstrated causal or out-of-sample edges.
educational_lesson.mathematics: Own proposed model: p_target_given_route ~ Beta(alpha,beta); after T targets on R eligible routes, posterior mean = (T+alpha)/(R+alpha+beta). This is a conditional binomial approximation, not a claim that NFL routes are independent or identically distributed. Estimate route-count scenarios separately and use E[T_next] = E[R_next * p_next], retaining dependence when roles change.
educational_lesson.synthetic_example: Teaching inputs only: 6 targets on 15 routes is 40%. A prespecified Beta(4,16) prior yields 10/35 = 28.57%; at 20 future routes the simple conditional expectation is 5.71 targets, rather than 8. These invented parameters are not Cowing, Waller or Mayer forecasts. The prior strength must be trained before evaluation, not selected to manufacture a desired answer.
assumptions: Consistent definitions for eligible routes and targets.
Historical prior exchangeability by position/role must be tested; role changes can invalidate it.
Target events share quarterback, game script and opponent conditions; use game-clustered evaluation.
Absent players and subminimum-route weeks remain in the candidate log, not silently removed.
challenged_assumptions: High TPRR guarantees a high-volume role.
A percentile gap guarantees positive regression in fantasy points.
An injury to a teammate identifies one certain beneficiary.
A transparent educator chart is an audited prediction model.
educational_lesson.evidence_grade: A for arithmetic and beta-binomial identity under stated assumptions; B for explanatory source transparency; C for untested predictive benefit.

expert_disagreement.text: The reviewed educators agree that route access matters; no independently verified head-to-head Cowing ranking disagreement was established. The substantive methodological tension is descriptive hot tiers/percentile gaps versus uncertainty-aware forecasts. Preserve model disagreement rather than treating a tier label as proof. A percentile gap is dimensionless and can reflect target depth, scoring, role or selection effects instead of future improvement.

research_proposals.name: Shrinkage plus explicit route scenarios improves next-game target forecasts
research_proposals.mechanism: Small-route extremes regress, while injuries affect future route access separately from target propensity.
research_proposals.testing_method: Freeze a recent-target baseline, raw-TPRR model and shrinkage/scenario model on the same candidates before kickoff. Fit priors and route filters on earlier weeks only. Evaluate held-out next-week target MAE, predictive interval coverage and proper distributional score; retain zero-route weeks and report them separately. Cluster uncertainty by game. Stratify TE/WR/RB, injury replacements and stable roles; log every failed hypothesis.
research_proposals.failure_condition: Reject deployment if chronological held-out error or coverage fails to improve, gains disappear when zero-route/inactive cases are retained, or success requires tuning on evaluation weeks.
research_proposals.implementation: Proposal only; review evidence before changing any controlling rule.
